text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Senior leaders of the opposition Socialist Party have called on the current party leadership to quit after the opposition's defeat in this month's municipal elections.
- The Central Election Commission ignored suggestions made by Italian observers which had asked for local elections to be repeated in several areas where they noted irregularities.
- A U.S. State Department official said Albania's local elections marked a step forward on the road towards democracy.
- Hajdin Sejdia, an ethnic Albanian Yugoslav businessman, faces arrest over the alleged mismanagement of Italian food aid if he returns to Albania, prosecutors say.
- A polio virus, which has already killed 12 people, has reappeared. Three people were hospitalized.
- Albania's trade unions look poised to stage a two-day strike to demand full compensations for increases in bread, fuel and transport prices.
- An ammunition plant in the central region of Elbasan has shut down, forcing its 600 workers to rely on a social assistance scheme.

- A petition from the traditional Socialist stronghold of Skrapari demanded the sacking of jailed Socialist leader Fatos Nano from his party rank and the rehabilitation of his deputy, Servet Pellumbi.
- The Monarchy Party, who won the northern town of Shkoder city hall in municipal elections, says it will start collecting signatures for the return of the pretender to the Albanian throne.
- Private enterprises are cropping up quickly in Albania but they meet serious difficulties, and the rate of failure is relatively high.
- A Japanese company is searching for chrome deposits in the hitherto unexplored region of Shebenik in eastern Albania.
- More than 75 percent of Albania's youth are in favour of the country's membership in the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, a poll shows.
